actions: Snapshot ipText and reset per-call parsing variables.
Treat the visible text as the bytes before the first NUL. Read at most 254 bytes using platform-supported, bounds-checked STRING access.
Process each visible byte once. Accept only ASCII digits and periods.
For a digit d, reject if octet > 25 or octet = 25 and d > 5; otherwise set octet := octet * 10 + d and mark the segment nonempty.
For a period, reject if the segment is empty or three periods have already occurred. Otherwise append the octet to candidate, increment the period count, and reset octet and the nonempty flag.
Append an octet using candidate := candidate * 256 + UDINT(octet). At each append the operation fits in UDINT.
transitions: READ -> REJECT on an invalid byte, invalid period, or out-of-range octet.
READ -> FINALIZE at the end of visible text.
FINALIZE -> ACCEPT if there are exactly three periods and the final segment is nonempty; append its octet to candidate.
ACCEPT -> COMMIT in the same invocation.
REJECT -> COMMIT in the same invocation.

actions: Assign the selected result to ipValue in the unified output stage.
transitions: COMMIT -> START on the next invocation; no parsing state is retained.

priorities: Malformed, non-ASCII, incomplete, or out-of-range visible text selects zero in the same invocation, overriding any previous output.
Valid text produces the four octets in network byte order; 0.0.0.0 legitimately produces zero.
Allow arbitrary leading zeros within the 254-byte capacity; do not enforce a 15-character visible-length limit.

The input interface or its ingress adapter must enforce the 254-byte capacity before NUL truncation. An already silently truncated over-capacity source cannot be detected reliably by this function block.

actions: Snapshot ipText at invocation; no edge detection is required.

actions: Reset per-call variables, then complete the bounded parse and select either candidate or zero.
All conceptual parsing transitions complete in this invocation; invalidity overrides the candidate.
